newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia May palm oil output seen up three pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia May palm oil output seen up three pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in May is expected to rise by three percent to 758,000 tonnes over April, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Tuesday.
Wong projected palm oil stocks at the end of May at 725,000-730,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 697,714 tonnes at end-April.
Exports in May were expected at 600,000-605,000 tonnes against 570,067 tonnes in April.

In a report, Wong said he expected only minor relief in the tight crude palm oil supply situation in Peninsular Malaysia in May-June as crude palm oil arrivals from eastern Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak were projected to improve by not more than 10,000 tonnes a month during the period.
"This is based on our estimate of modest month-on-month increases in crude palm oil output," he said.
